page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.6xlarge is a high clock speed, compute-oriented instance provisioned via the KVM hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 24 dedicated virtual CPUs backed by an Intel Xeon 6149 processor operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz. The instance is allocated 48.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This configuration targets tasks requiring strong per-thread execution capability and high CPU core density rather than expansive in-memory storage.

The instance does not include integrated local storage, requiring all persistent storage and operating system volumes to be provisioned via remote block storage. For network communication, ecs.hfc5.6xlarge provides a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The hardware footprint omits dedicated GPU accelerators. Architectural tradeoffs center on the low memory-to-core ratio and the reliance on external network volumes for input/output operations, which can bound I/O throughput depending on the attached storage tier.

From a resource efficiency perspective, the dedicated high-frequency CPU cores combined with a 1:2 RAM ratio offer balanced efficiency for computationally dense workloads that do not require high memory footprints. Workload fits include batch processing, distributed build environments, continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) pipelines, front-end web application clusters, and scientific simulation jobs that depend on elevated single-core clock frequencies and multi-threaded scaling.
